blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — A group of pork producers urges the government to reclassify frozen pork jowls as swine meat, arguing that the tariff gap disrupts the local industry and gives imported pork cuts an undue advantage. The Pork Producers Federation of the Philippines Inc. (ProPork) pushes to remove the current tariff treatment for standalone imported pork jowls and instead apply the 30-percent in-quota and 40-percent out-quota tariff rates. READ: US group warns vs pork jowl tariff shift ProPork wants the government to classify standalone pork jowls, imported separately from the pig’s head, as pork meat.
